description: Final accepted unlettered body prompts. Mini top switch and external USB were subsequently removed manually at the user's explicit request.

prompts.mini: A faithful product photograph-style render of a small DIY electronic pocket calculator. Brown plain studio background, soft light, straight front view, landscape 16:9 frame. The device is square, matte-black layered PCB panels, held by black corner screws. A blank yellow-green LCD1602 two-line display in a black rectangular bezel takes the upper third. A small amber LED sits below the display on the right. A SMALL BLACK POWER SLIDE SWITCH projects upright from the centre of the top edge of the square body. The right edge is bare with a small empty USB socket, absolutely nothing plugged in: no USB plug or cable. The lower half is a precise 8-column by 5-row keyboard grid marked by thin white cell borders. In each of the forty cells is a TINY BLACK STANDARD TACTILE SWITCH ACTUATOR, a thin straight cylinder about 3mm in diameter, with a small flat round top. The actuator diameter is only 20 percent of each cell width, leaving nearly all of the cell as empty black label space. These are thin stems coming through holes in the front panel, NOT big caps, not wide rims and not domes. All40 actuators have the same small size. No printed text, letters, numbers or logos, display uniformly blank. No circuit decoration or accessories. Entire device visible and centred; square body is 82% of the canvas height.
prompts.classic: A faithful clean studio rendering of a DIY electronic calculator. Plain deep warm brown background. Straight front view, landscape 16:9 composition, soft top-left studio light. The calculator is a vertical rectangle, width 0.60 times height, centred and fully visible, 82 percent of canvas height. Its front panel is completely PLAIN RED, held by simple black corner screws. At the top is a blank green-grey graphical LCD with a simple black bezel. A plain red strip below the screen is reserved for a later model name. Below are forty tiny black round standard tactile-switch plungers in FIVE columns by EIGHT rows. Each plunger is a narrow straight cylindrical stem with a small flat top: diameter only ONE QUARTER of a cell width, like a standard 3mm actuator, about 20 image pixels. All remaining space in each cell is empty red space for typography. Thin white rectangular grid lines divide the cells. NO large button caps, no broad bevel or flange. IMPORTANT: the entire red front panel has NO gold or copper traces, NO gold dots or patterns, NO decorative lines and NO extra electronic parts. Only red substrate, black screws, screen and the white keyboard grid. No lettering anywhere, no USB cables, no accessories. The image should accurately show small standard tactile-switch actuators, not consumer keyboard keycaps.
prompts.40th: Refine the buttons of this electronic calculator rendering to match thin flat physical pushbuttons. Keep exact body, screws, screen, headers, warm brown background, lighting, forty button centres and all colours. Reduce every round button from the current diameter ~60 pixels to diameter ~35 pixels (about 35% of the centre pitch). Make their tops FLAT and their visible height LOW: short cylindrical pushbuttons with a very slight bevel, not domed puffy keycaps or pills. Preserve the same 8 columns by 5 rows and the white/green/blue/red colours in their current positions. Leave plenty of empty panel around each button for manual labels. Blank screen and no text anywhere. Do not change anything else.
